statement: A number has two digits. Its digits add to 9, and the digit on the left is twice the digit on the right. What is the number?

choices.misconception: I made the digits add to 9 but got the doubling the wrong way round.
I made the digits add to 9 but did not check the doubling clue.
I made the left digit the bigger one, but 5 is not twice 4.
I made the left digit twice the right one but forgot the digits must add to 9.

hints: List every pair of digits that adds to nine.
Write out the pairs that add to 9, then test each pair against the second clue. Only one pair has a left digit that is exactly double the right digit.
The pairs adding to 9 are 1 and 8, 2 and 7, 3 and 6, 4 and 5, and each of those the other way round.

solutions.reliable: The digit pairs adding to 9 are 1 and 8, 2 and 7, 3 and 6, 4 and 5, in either order. Only 6 and 3 has the left digit twice the right, so the number is 63. The idea to keep: use the first clue to make a short list, then test the list against the second clue rather than guessing.

whyOnTest: Checking a short list against a second clue is how early digit puzzles are solved, and every distractor satisfies one clue but not both.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
